entities.summary:
Jerónimo Xavierre (1546, Zaragoza – 1608-09-08, Madrid) was a Spanish Dominican theologian and Master General of his order, whose career spanned the late 16th and early 17th centuries, a period marked by intense Catholic Counter-Reformation efforts and theological debates within the Iberian Peninsula and Rome. His leadership significantly influenced the internal discipline and intellectual direction of the Dominican Order during a crucial phase of consolidation after the Council of Trent, positioning it as a bulwark against Protestant ideas while navigating complex relationships with the Spanish Crown and the Papacy. He engaged with prominent intellectual currents, notably the Thomistic revival, and contributed to the spiritual and administrative vigor of one of Catholicism's most influential religious orders.

Elected Master General of the Order of Preachers (Dominicans) in 1601, Xavierre oversaw a period of administrative reform, emphasizing strict adherence to the Constitutions of the Order and promoting scholastic rigor. He actively intervened in the *De Auxiliis* controversy, a heated theological dispute concerning divine grace and free will between Dominicans and Jesuits, advocating for the traditional Thomistic position against Molinist doctrines. His tenure included extensive visitations of Dominican provinces across Europe, reinforcing monastic discipline and intellectual standards, and he worked to establish new convents and strengthen existing ones, particularly in Spain and its expanding colonial territories.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jerónimo Xavierre's leadership as Master General of the Dominican Order solidified its post-Tridentine structure and intellectual identity, ensuring its continued influence in Catholic theology and missionary efforts into the 17th century. His defense of Thomism in major theological debates had lasting implications for Dominican scholarship.
